ideas.title: Window assignment prefers colour-imbalanced windows as handles (revive gproxy's B term under reset6)
ideas.mechanism: hcost(j) = 1.52*m*(M + r/2)/(M + m + r) with m/M = minority/majority hole counts of handle j and r = reset_strength*nt. At a balanced handle (m = M) the value is 0.76*m for every r, but at an imbalanced handle it falls with r: for 70/30 holes and nt = 10 it is 30.4 at r = 2nt and 28.5 at r = 6nt, versus 38.0 for 50/50 at both. So after reset6 the anneal profits more from handles whose upstream targets are mostly one colour. The anneal already optimises the handle depth order (handle swap, 150 per mille of moves) and the column assignment of targets, but the choice of WHICH 25 of the 63 active windows become handles is made only by gobj (pair matching cost), which is colour-blind: a window with 140/116 ones/zeros among the 256 barcodes is a better handle than a 128/128 one because its upstream minority can be made smaller, and gobj does not see it. A pair's handle differences add one hole of each colour, so the pair price itself needs no colour term; only the handle-set term is missing.
ideas.change: In assign_windows (solutions/d30a-reset6/main.cpp): precompute, as in solutions/as6-gproxy/main.cpp l.855-870, bias_table[8][256] from the public barcodes (per window w: (ones_w - 128)^2 / H), and add lambda * sum over the 8 bytes of the handle mask of bias_table[b][(handle_mask >> 8b) & 255] to the objective returned by both matching_cost lambdas (l.1491 and l.1568; the handle_mask is already a parameter) in the same 1/3600 integer key units as gobj (lambda = 0.001 moves per unit of B = 3.6 key units; also try 0.002). The term only changes on window role swaps (as_names 'window'), so the loss screens and pair caches are untouched. Drop gproxy's S term (pair-difference spread), which the anneal's handle swap already covers.
ideas.evidence: as6-gproxy README: within-input correlation of the assignment objective with the final model_cost 0.575 -> 0.756 when B and S are added; trial_log l.335: as6-gproxy alone -0.052 +- 0.026 % (20261103-032506) on as6-imb0gb, but as6-cg (with as6-canon) +0.027 % so it was dropped (net about -0.01 %). hcost shape computed from Design::hole_cost_of l.2746 and refresh_reset l.2755 of d30a-reset6. Handle order is annealed (move mix l.3405 'handle swap 150'); the window set is fixed at map_end.
ideas.prior_attempts: as6-gproxy / astra-gproxy (11-03, under reset 2 and before assign-search elite paths, loss screens and the dual30 pipeline): -0.052 % alone, net about -0.01 % with canon, not adopted. left-hclimb (11-01, handle order) accepted 0 moves: closed, and now subsumed by the anneal's handle swaps. Never retested on the dcomp line, and reset6 is the new reason: the objective now rewards imbalance at handles more than at the time gproxy was dropped.
ideas.evaluation: dv_best proxy on 500 seeds for lambda in {0.001, 0.002} against d30a-reset6 (same seeds, --compare so gobj/handle stats are paired); keep the lambda with dv_best lower by >= 2 SE and gobj_after not worse by more than 0.02 (gobj is about 3 %/unit). Then --compare solutions/d30a-reset6 solutions/if6-gobj-bias on 2000 seeds; adopt at <= -0.03 % (2 SE = 0.044 %).
ideas.probe: 500-seed --compare of reset6 vs lambda 0.001 and 0.002; read dv_best, gobj_after, and the mean per-handle minority share from @paper/@ops replays (or the hcost sum in the chosen_log) to confirm the handles became more imbalanced and V fell.
ideas.risks: gobj loses pair quality (gobj about 3 %/unit): too large a lambda trades real generic-layer moves for a proxy; the as6-cg stacking result (+0.027 %) shows the gain can vanish with other changes. Port risk: the dual30 matching_cost is radix-sorted branch-free code with cached keys; the term must be added after the matching sum, not inside the per-pair keys.

ideas.title: reset_strength scheduled over the 4 anneal segments (2 -> 6 ramp or 6 -> 10) instead of one constant
ideas.mechanism: With r = 6 nt the hole cost is almost linear in the minority count (0.76*m*(M + r/2)/(M + m + r)), i.e. majority holes are nearly free: many moves have small or zero hole deltas and the landscape is flatter, which is good for the final fine-tuning but gives the hot shared segments less guidance on where to put balanced handles. A per-segment schedule lets segments 0-1 (shared prefix, temperature 2.0 -> about 0.17) use the smoother r = 2-4 nt landscape and the branches (segments 2-3) the sharp r = 6 nt one; the last segment keeps 6 so refresh_reset's final reset_targets (used by the rematch's hole gradient l.4065) are unchanged. The reverse direction (6 in the prefix, 8-10 in the branches) tests whether the saturation seen for a global 8/10 was only the prefix's fault.
ideas.change: Design::refresh_reset (l.2755) takes the segment index: reset_targets[c] = reset_mult[seg] * nt[c] with reset_mult = {2, 4, 6, 6} (variant A) or {6, 6, 10, 10} (variant B); the call at l.2925 in Design::anneal passes the segment; the call before filler_climb (l.3589) and in rematch_probability (l.4036) use the last multiplier (6) so finishing is identical to reset6. One constexpr array, LOCAL_BENCH env for the four values.
ideas.evidence: impla-notes PROGRESS.md: reset 4 -> V -0.0037 +- 0.0019, reset 6 -0.0053, reset 8 -0.0050, reset 10 -0.0042 (500 seeds, 20261109-100936 / 115802): V improves up to 6 and saturates; score reset6 -0.086 % GCC (20261109-114428), reset8/10 not better (115802). Nothing in the log varies the reset within the anneal; the segments already exist (kAnnealSegments 4, refresh per segment).
ideas.prior_attempts: Only global constants were tried (reset 2, 4, 6, 8, 10; today). 8 segments (d30a-seg8) made V worse, but that changed the refresh frequency, not the strength. No segment-dependent hcost parameter has been tried.
ideas.evaluation: dv_best proxy on 500 seeds for variants A and B vs d30a-reset6 (paired --compare); continue only if a variant lowers dv_best by >= 2 SE (about 0.004); then 2000-seed --compare vs d30a-reset6, adopt at <= -0.03 %.
ideas.probe: The 500-seed dv_best run itself (two variants plus the base, about 6 minutes of lock time).
ideas.risks: The reset saturation (6 vs 8/10 equal within noise) suggests the objective is already on a plateau, so the schedule may be flat too; variant A changes the shared prefix for all 9 candidates and could lower the branch diversity V selects from.

ideas.title: Even reset split at tied hole counts in head_probability (ride-along rule fix for the perforation/rematch reset)
ideas.mechanism: Design::head_probability (l.2749) gives the whole reset demand to colour 0 when x == y ('y > x' is false), so at tied handles the predicted head is colour 0 with probability (x + r)/(2x + r), a bias with no basis in the solver. It feeds the filler climb (2.0 nt), the rematch's ProbabilityHead and the perforation's head samples (2*demands). Any change that raises those reset strengths to 6 (the sub-floor perforation variant, -0.029 % GCC) triples the bias; splitting the reset evenly removes it. Ties are frequent only at shallow handles (few holes), so the effect is small.
ideas.change: l.2749: p = (y + reset * ((y > x) + .5 * (y == x))) / n (done in solutions/if6-eventie). Stack it with the perforation reset 2 -> 6 variant (Perforation l.9881: 2 * demands -> 6 * demands) in one candidate.
ideas.evidence: Probe 20261109-131412_d30a-reset6 vs 20261109-131412_if6-eventie, 200 seeds: score +0.012 +- 0.034 % (95/3/102, n.s.; only a minority of designs change), mean dv_best 10.0384 -> 10.0372 (-0.0012), req_sec +2.6 ms (noise). Perforation reset 6: -0.029 % GCC / -0.007 % Clang (the other proposer's screening, below the floor).
ideas.prior_attempts: The tie rule has never been touched (same formula since the head_probability was introduced; V's probabilities l.10135 has the same tie rule and is left alone because V was fit with it). Perforation reset 6 was screened today and is sub-floor alone.
ideas.evaluation: Not worth a run alone. Include in the perforation-reset-6 candidate and judge that stack with a 2000-seed --compare vs d30a-reset6; adopt the stack only at <= -0.03 %.
ideas.probe: Already run (200 seeds); a 500-seed dv_best of the stack (eventie + perforation 6) before the 2000-seed compare.
ideas.risks: Pure noise at this size; adds nothing if the perforation-6 stack is not pursued.

proposals.notes:
Audit of the hcost-coupled rules (d30a-reset6 main.cpp): (1) hcost = 1.52(xy + 0.5 r min(x,y))/(x+y+r) is exactly the Markov model 'head flips to the demanded colour on a mismatch, resets to the majority colour at rate r', i.e. x*p1 + y*p0 with head_probability's p; the min term and the 0.5 are not free knobs but consequences of that model, so sweeping them separately is not meaningful. The actual effect of reset 2 -> 6 is modest in shape: balanced handles cost 0.76*x for any r, imbalanced handles get about 6 % cheaper, and the dependence on nt (column size) triples. (2) Already screened by the other agent with no gain: kHoleWeight, generic/column scales, climb proxy weight, rematch weights, perforation profit weight, climb/rematch probability reset 6; perforation reset 6 sub-floor. (3) Pair pricing colour-blindness (gobj 0.5*hd, initialize 0.65*hd) is NOT stale: a pair difference at a handle adds one hole of each colour, so min(x,y) rises by exactly 1 and the price is colour-independent; search-hd (trial_log l.279, l.299) found 1500-1800 flat. (4) initialize's colour-balanced column seeding (2*n1<nc alternate fill, 3*|..| term): removal of the alternation gave no difference (trial_log l.332) and the anneal's unit moves re-sort; not proposed. (5) V's probabilities(2.) in add_stationary_features: a rescale to 6 changes the DP2 features V was fitted on; dv_best cannot evaluate a V change and a refit (7 designs x 8 order lists x 500 seeds) does not fit the 14:45 window: rejected for today. (6) Refresh lag of reset_targets within a segment is 3x larger in effect under reset6, but seg8 (8 refreshes, same work) made V worse today, so not re-proposed.

Rejected by probe: if6-nocorr (drop the colcost correction '+np-1 when all pairs of a column share one handle colour', both scalar least_depths2 l.2733 and the SIMD colcost_pair l.2975): 200 seeds 20261109-130516_d30a-reset6 vs 20261109-130516_if6-nocorr: +0.772 +- 0.076 % (45/2/153), req_sec +17 ms, dv_best 10.0384 -> 10.0633 (+0.025). The rule is strongly load-bearing: the request side (fix_handles digging to a paper of the other colour, the initial column order DP) relies on the other colour sitting second, so this is not a stale cyclic-era rule and should not be touched; if anything the opposite (a graded penalty when the minority colour of a column is thin) is the only untested direction, not proposed for lack of time. Note V underestimates such request-side harm about 30x (0.025 V vs 0.77 % real), so dv_best proxies of rules that touch the column colour structure must be confirmed by score.

Probe dirs: solutions/if6-nocorr (IF6_CORR=1 restores), solutions/if6-eventie. Both based on d30a-reset6, LOCAL_BENCH switches, READMEs present. No commits.

ideas.title: Raise the filler cover credit kCoverStrength 0.25 -> ~0.45 (keep kStayStrength 0.25)
ideas.mechanism: reset6 designs hold their head colours better (stats 20261109-114428: fix moves 1.542 -> 1.484 per order, model_hole 3.94 -> 3.79) while fillers are returned more (fret 1.199 -> 1.239). A filler left below the generic layer that covers handle holes (stay_table cover) therefore saves relatively more future handle fixes than on the old designs, but adaptive_next_cost only credits it with kCoverStrength = 0.25 of the hole rate (main.cpp l.5047/5218/5501/5547, constant at l.4865). On the old designs this constant was flat (trial_log l.436: |diff| <= 0.003 %); on reset6 designs it is not: 0.35 gives -0.013 +- 0.003 %, 0.45 gives -0.020 +- 0.005 %. The stay-probability term in filler_charge (kStayStrength, l.4916) and its threshold 0.3 are NOT the lever: stay-only .35 -0.008 +- 0.005, threshold .4 +0.060, threshold .25 ~0, both .5/.5 +0.045 (stay too high hurts).
ideas.change: solutions/d30a-reset6/main.cpp l.4865: `static constexpr double kStayStrength = .25, kCoverStrength = .25;` -> keep kStayStrength .25, set kCoverStrength to the best of {0.45, 0.55, 0.65} (0.45 is the best measured so far and the curve was still falling: .25 -> .35 -> .45 = 0 / -0.013 / -0.020 %). The constant enters adaptive_next_cost (scalar l.5047, AVX2 l.5210/5218, column-MDP partial/term l.5501/5547) and the covered[] credit only; no new work, so request time is unchanged. Note the comment at l.5198 claims exactness on a 1/1024 grid for .25 and integer depths: with .45 the SIMD checkpoint sums are no longer exactly representable, so check that NEXT_PREFIX_CHECK (ref vs SIMD) still agrees within its tolerance, or pick 0.5 if an exact binary fraction is required (0.5 was NOT probed with stay .25; .5/.5 was worse only because of the stay term).
ideas.prior_attempts: trial_log l.436 (2026-11-04 planner tune, old designs): kStayStrength/kCoverStrength within +-0.003 %, stay threshold 0.4 -> 0.3 -0.003 % (l.435). Never re-swept after the column MDP (11-05) or on reset6 designs. The stay threshold was re-probed here (0.25 / 0.4): leave it at 0.3.
ideas.evaluation: (1) --compare solutions/d30a-reset6 vs cover .45 / .55 / .65 (stay .25) with --design-from on B's saved *_d30a-reset6 run (or --extend 20261109-130040_d30a-reset6 to 2000 seeds with --save-design) --orders 4, 2000 seeds (SE ~0.0015 %); take the best value, adopt if <= -0.015 % at >= 2 SE. (2) Normal --compare d30a-reset6 vs the winner, 2000 seeds, to confirm no regression (the design-side noise, SE 0.026 %, cannot resolve 0.02 %; the rule is 'not worse than +0.03 %' and req_sec unchanged).
ideas.probe: Already run: 200 seeds x 4 orders on fixed designs (above). Cheapest next step: the 3-value sweep at 500 seeds x 4 orders (~2 min of cases).
ideas.probe_result: cover .35 -0.013 +- 0.003 % (20261109-130755_if7-coveronly035), cover .45 -0.020 +- 0.005 % (20261109-131139_if7-coveronly045), stay .30/cover .40 -0.017 +- 0.005 % (20261109-131139_if7-stay030cover040); negatives: .5/.5 +0.045 % (20261109-130755_if7-stay050), threshold .4 +0.060 % (20261109-130755_if7-stay035thr040). Sources in solutions/if7-coveronly035, if7-coveronly045, if7-stay030cover040, if7-stay050, if7-stay035thr040, if7-stay035thr025, if7-cover035thr025, if7-stayonly035, if7-stay035.
ideas.risks: Below the 0.03 % merge floor on its own (stack it with another request-side step or with reset6 itself). The gain is measured on one set of 200 saved designs; 2000 seeds may shrink it (the stay/cover constants were flat on the old designs, so the effect is design-dependent by construction). The SIMD next_cost assumes exact 1/1024-grid arithmetic for .25; a non-dyadic constant may change prefix-check tolerances (choose 0.5 if that matters).

ideas.title: Re-sweep the neutral-search budget (NEUTRAL_SLACK, NEUTRAL_WIDTH, REPEAT_MIN) on reset6 designs
ideas.mechanism: On reset6 designs the neutral search is more productive: neutral_accepted 29.1 -> 31.1 per case (+7 %), ns_one_accepts 925 -> 965 (+4 %), ns_changed 387 -> 403, repair moves 0.645 -> 0.683 per order, tie_switches 221 -> 234. The marginal value of one more neutral candidate / a wider slack therefore rose, while the budget constants (search_env l.6959-6972: NEUTRAL_SLACK 0.30, NEUTRAL_WIDTH 6, REPEAT_MIN 0.05) were set on alt1/dual25 designs where they were just below the design rate (0.025-0.046 %/100 ms vs 0.03).
ideas.change: solutions/d30a-reset6/main.cpp search_env l.6959-6972: NEUTRAL_SLACK 0.30 -> 0.35, NEUTRAL_WIDTH 6 -> 8, REPEAT_MIN 0.05 -> 0.0 as three separate variants (the F3_<NAME> env vars allow this without code copies if the evaluation inherits the environment; otherwise one-line edits).
ideas.evidence: stats 20261109-114428_d30a-reset6 --vs 20261109-114428_dcomp-combo-dual30 (neutral_accepted, ns_one_accepts, repair label). Prior rates on alt1 (REPORT11, fixed 500x4): slack .5 -0.0028 % (+10.5 ms), width 12 -0.0051 % (+11 ms), REPEAT_MIN 0 -0.0058 % (+22.8 ms).
ideas.prior_attempts: REPORT11 table (trial_log 2026-11-08 sections, dcomp-notes): slack .35 0.068 %/100 ms on legal-tie-fast, slack .5 / width 12 / REPEAT_MIN 0 all 0.025-0.046 %/100 ms on alt1 (sub-rate, not closed by principle; map section 5.5). Not re-measured on dual30 or reset6 designs.
ideas.evaluation: --compare d30a-reset6 vs the 3 variants --design-from (saved reset6 designs) --orders 4, 500 seeds (SE ~0.003 %); adopt a variant only if its gain per 100 ms of req_sec exceeds 0.03 %/100 ms (the design rate the final version pays), i.e. >= 0.004 % for +12 ms, and stack it with cover-credit-045.
ideas.probe: The 500x4 fixed-design compare above is the probe (about 3 min of cases for 4 solutions).
ideas.risks: Each variant costs request time that the final version must take from the design budget; the measured rates were marginal before and the increase in neutral productivity is only +4-7 %, so the expected gain is small (0.003-0.01 %). Pacer tail (end_sec > 1.8 s) grows with request time.

ideas.title: Refit the near-tie correction (kTieConst/kTieCoef) on reset6 designs
ideas.mechanism: The 9 ridge coefficients (l.8731-8732) were fit on rollout labels from deval-helper-wide designs (reset 2, before flex125/warm refinish/reset6). On reset6 designs the correction fires more (tie_switches 221 -> 234 per case, +6 %, tie_decisions unchanged 700 -> 705), and its largest coefficients price exactly the quantities that moved: filler_charge x1.32 (fret +0.04 moves/order), next_cost x0.19, #fillers below the generic layer -0.10, head opposite-colour demand -0.145 (head colours are more stable now). A refit with the same pipeline (legal-roll-feat: rollouts on seeds 0-99 under the reset6 policy) re-aligns the correction with the new head/filler statistics.
ideas.change: Rerun the legal-roll-feat labelling (solutions/legal-roll-feat: rollout alternatives within kTieGap, ridge on the 9 tie_features) with solutions/d30a-reset6 as the policy and reset6 designs, then replace kTieConst and kTieCoef at main.cpp l.8731-8732. No structural change.
ideas.evidence: stats 20261109-114428 (tie_switches, tie_decisions, fret/fix label shifts); trial_log 2026-11-08 legal-tie-fix section (-0.068 % on fit designs; refit on dual25 +0.006 %).
ideas.prior_attempts: legal-tie-fix (11-08) fit on deval-helper-wide; refit on dual25 designs gave +0.006 % (worse); extra features n.s.; policy iteration converged (+0.0001 moves/decision). The dual25 refit failure suggests the fit is saturated unless the designs changed materially - reset6 is the first design change that moved the tie statistics by > 5 %.
ideas.evaluation: --compare d30a-reset6 vs the refit --design-from (saved reset6 designs) --orders 4, 2000 seeds; adopt only at <= -0.005 % and >= 2 SE, stacked with cover-credit-045.
ideas.probe: Before refitting: check the current correction's calibration on reset6 designs by counting tie_switches that raised vs lowered the realised cost in 50 rollouts (the legal-roll-feat tooling); if the switch accuracy equals the 11-08 figure, skip the refit.
ideas.risks: The dual25 refit was worse; a refit on 100 seeds of labels can overfit and the 2.5-hour budget is tight for rollouts + ridge + 2000-seed compare. Lowest priority of the four.

ideas.title: Re-sweep the column-MDP mixing weights (mix/drop 0.5, next_mix 0.5) on reset6 designs
ideas.mechanism: reset6 designs have smaller deep columns and more MDP coverage: colmdp_full_states 20076 -> 16400, colmdp_sequences 71398 -> 58970, colmdp_columns 24.907 -> 24.955, partial_mdp_hits 253k -> 123k (the uncovered-column slow path is used half as often). The MDP's handle-demand events (rate lambda_b, cost = depth of the first paper of that colour) are design-derived, but the share of the one-step model replaced by F/H (ColMdpConfig l.4527-4530: mix 0.5, keep 0.5, next_mix 0.5) was tuned on 11-05 designs where head fixes were 4 % more frequent. With steadier heads the sequence-value F should be trusted a little more (mix/next_mix 0.6) or the barrier 'keep' less.
ideas.change: solutions/d30a-reset6/main.cpp ColMdpConfig l.4527-4530: variants mix 0.5 -> 0.6, next_mix 0.5 -> 0.6, keep 0.5 -> 0.35 (three one-line variants; env overrides exist if ColMdpConfig reads env_real).
ideas.evidence: stats 20261109-114428_d30a-reset6 --vs dual30: colmdp_* and partial_mdp_* counters above. trial_log l.1513: next_mix .25/.75 +0.086/+0.005 % on 11-05 designs (asymmetric: .75 nearly flat, so the optimum may sit above 0.5).
ideas.prior_attempts: Column MDP added 11-05 (-0.100 % alone); next_mix 0.25/0.75 +0.086/+0.005 % (trial_log l.1513); covering all columns -0.0009 % (argon-des-colmdp); heavy-mdp settings at 5-10x time. No sweep of mix/keep since 11-05 and none on reset6 designs.
ideas.evaluation: --compare d30a-reset6 vs 3 variants --design-from (saved reset6 designs) --orders 4, 500 seeds (SE ~0.003 %); adopt the best only if <= -0.006 % at >= 2 SE, then confirm at 2000 seeds stacked with cover-credit-045.
ideas.probe: The 500x4 compare is the probe (3 min of cases).
ideas.risks: The 11-05 result 'the shape of the value matters, not its scale' means constant rescaling may do nothing; expected gain is small and may be zero.

proposals.notes: Method: compared the stderr metrics of 20261109-114428_d30a-reset6 vs 20261109-114428_dcomp-combo-dual30 (2000 seeds) and probed request-side constants on 200 saved reset6 designs (run 20261109-130040_d30a-reset6, --save-design, seeds 0-199) with --design-from --orders 4 (SE 0.002-0.008 %). Three compare groups: 20261109-130415, 20261109-130755, 20261109-131139 (all request-only, not recorded in pahcer/). Probe sources are in solutions/if7-* (each with README). What moved on reset6 designs: fix moves -0.058/order, fret +0.040, repair +0.038, neutral_accepted +7 %, tie_switches +6 %, colmdp_full_states -18 %, partial_mdp_hits -51 %; helper usage unchanged (help 0.075 vs 0.074, helper_papers -1 %), so I do not propose touching the helper menu sizes. Rejected after probing: kFillerCharge 0.65 / 0.75 = +0.027 +- 0.007 / +0.122 +- 0.008 % (20261109-130415_if7-charge065 / if7-charge075) - 0.7 stays optimal on reset6 designs, same as on dual25 (REPORT12); kFillerDemandWeight 0.40 = -0.001 +- 0.002 % (20261109-130415_if7-demand040) - flat; stay threshold 0.3 -> 0.4 = +0.060 % and -> 0.25 = ~0 (if7-stay035thr040 / if7-stay035thr025, if7-cover035thr025) - leave at 0.3; kStayStrength alone .35 = -0.008 +- 0.005 (if7-stayonly035) and .5/.5 = +0.045 (if7-stay050) - the stay term is not the lever, the cover credit in adaptive_next_cost is. The handle-fix costs (handle_fix_cost l.5697) and adaptive_holes are design-derived, so they adapt to reset6 automatically; nothing stale found there. Not probed for lack of time: kEndWeight on reset6 designs (prior: every value other than 1.0 lost; 1.05 -0.0055 % at +13.5 ms on dual25), alternate_gap > 1.0 (sub-rate before). Caveat on the main idea: the design-side 2000-seed compare cannot resolve 0.02 % (SE 0.026 %); the implementer should rely on the fixed-design 2000x4 compare for the decision and use the normal compare only as a no-regression check. Time cost of cover-credit-045 is 0 by construction (a constant inside the same arithmetic); the +11 ms seen at 200 seeds is the usual spread of --design-from timings (variants with identical work differed by +-10 ms in the same groups).
